episode_title: Rotem Lurie (Venice Security) on Intuition, Sacrifice, and Leading as a Woman

real_qa.q: How did Rotem Lurie build confidence in her intuition as CEO of Venice Security?
real_qa.r: Rotem learned to trust her intuition primarily through experience with people decisions in business. She realized that early-stage technology is bought based on personal trust and relationships, not feature parity with competitors. Her confidence grew after repeatedly discovering that her gut instincts were correct, even when experienced advisors contradicted her. She states: 'the moment that I started to trust myself and my guts and my intuition, and again, the reason why it happened was because I've just realized that my intuition was right all along. Then I think we've also started to see the success.'
real_qa.requete: Rotem Lurie intuition confidence Venice Security

real_qa.q: What role did Unit 8200 play in shaping the Israeli cybersecurity founder ecosystem?
real_qa.r: Rotem explains that graduates from Unit 8200 often start companies after seeing peers achieve massive exits like 200 million dollar acquisitions, creating an 'Israeli dream' effect. She notes that this competitive drive from the 8200 community powers innovation and technology advancement in Israel, though she observes that as competition intensifies and you move higher in ranks, there are fewer women founders present.

real_qa.q: What sacrifices has Rotem Lurie made as founder and CEO of Venice Security?
real_qa.r: Rotem sacrificed her natural humility and modesty, becoming 'a little bit delusional' to make her vision real. She is relocating from Israel to the United States despite Israel being her home and where all her friends are. She has also surrendered her hobbies and personal time, stating: 'I was asked recently, what are my hobbies? What do I like to do? And I shit you not, I have no idea how to answer that. I don't know. I work.'
real_qa.requete: Rotem Lurie sacrifices hobbies founder lifestyle

real_qa.q: How did Asaf Rappaport's mentorship at Microsoft impact Rotem Lurie's career?
real_qa.r: Asaf Rappaport, who had sold Adalom to Microsoft (which became MCAS), became VP of the entire cloud security department after Rotem joined as a product intern on Azure Security Center. Despite being the youngest intern with limited experience, Asaf gave her access to projects and customers she would not normally have reached. When asked why he believed in her, Asaf never gave her a satisfactory explanation, but Rotem credits this opportunity with proving she could perform at advanced levels and shaped her career trajectory.
real_qa.requete: Asaf Rappaport Microsoft MCAS Adalom acquisition

real_qa.q: Why does Rotem Lurie remain driven to push further despite potential financial independence?
real_qa.r: Rotem explains that money is not her primary motivation on difficult days—it is the drive to push the bar further and prove herself capable of doing big things. She describes a constant voice in her head saying 'I'm going to show them' and acknowledges that for her, the satisfaction comes from conquering targets and achieving what she never imagined possible, like speaking to crowds of 1,000 people about cybersecurity despite not being a security researcher.
real_qa.requete: founder motivation money versus achievement drive

guest.bio_context: Rotem Lurie served in Unit 8200 of the Israeli Defense Force, later worked as a product intern at Microsoft in Azure Security Center under Asaf Rappaport, and was promoted to work on advanced projects with customers despite her junior status. She was the first in her officer training class to be selected for officer school, and her mother was the only woman accepted to Talpiot in her class, serving as a major inspiration for her career trajectory in technology.
